== Publication-history consolidation and remaining source gaps (#445) ==
Bill approved merging the Premium overview into [[Virtual Set 1: Legacy]] and redirecting its old URL on 14 November 2026. The Premium Edition section retains the original PDF link, icon-key explanation, date evidence and access to all twelve standalone Premium card articles. Their content and identifiers were not changed. The main card-list text and images are preserved; its two column labels now distinguish PC-remastered slips from wiki reconstructions. The existing Printings anchor remains available.

The four presentation groups are documented from cached primary sheets and the locally preserved 11 June 2002 Decipher card-list index. The index offered Set #1 and Set #1a side by side, with BB/WB printouts and an explicit Dark Side white-on-black option; “#1a” alone must not be treated as proof of a later gameplay erratum. The unnumbered PC #1a and numbered Decipher #1/#1a files are distinguishable payloads. Premium's footer year and PDF creation date do not establish its publication day/order. The 2006 sheet's official-text cutoff likewise differs from its metadata creation date and does not establish a release day.

The requested before/after evidence for Decipher's later withdrawal remains unresolved: the cached index establishes presence, but this bounded local corpus supplies no checked comparable absent page. No removal date, cause or claim that files were deleted is added. All Archive.org requests, including replays and CDX/status checks, remain paused at Bill's direction. Access can resume there only after his explicit authorization.

Original-set designer identities, reasons for the revisions and the date improved templates became available require additional primary evidence. The 2006 cover explicitly credits proofing and graphic-design teams, but its credits must not be projected backward onto the original 2002 card design. Existing metadata usernames remain leads rather than confirmed original designer credits. Existing later-era comparison/transcription issues from the earlier Set 1 audit remain tracked separately; this merge is not a fresh certification of every old game-text cell. Exact source/draft and live backups plus the redirect/anchor transfer map are retained with story #445. == Further launch history, website comparison and numbered print choices (#445) ==
Added the checked February/March 2002 reports and Decipher's 5 March announcement. A planned 4 March release is distinguished from the announcement's date and 9 March tournament legality. The first-spoiler report identifies Doug Taylor as posting the preview, but this does not identify every original designer; no unsupported designer attribution is added.

The 11 June 2002 index lists the Virtual section; the 2 October 2002 www-host index omits it. Both actual replays were opened and photographed at matching page positions. These bound the observed listing change between those captures; the www/non-www host difference is retained, so they do not establish an exact removal day, universal host synchronisation or a cause. They also do not establish deletion of the PDF files. The capture index returned a further changed digest in 2005; that is not itself evidence of the 2002 removal date.

The numbered #1 and #1a sheets have identical extracted text and statistics after their sheet-title difference is removed. All six Dark Side crops now show the black-on-white versus white-on-black choice explicitly. The earlier unnumbered PC #1a is a separate payload and must not be conflated with numbered Decipher #1a. Printing colour is a publication/presentation distinction, not evidence of another gameplay erratum. Existing numbered card articles/images need a separate per-family presentation audit before their Errata labels can be treated as accurate publication labels; no new gameplay IDs or additional card-family memberships are assigned here. The main article now exposes both original sheets and all six paired Dark Side slips instead of implying only one numbered presentation.

Bill clarified that Archive.org reading/downloads are allowed while uploads and save submissions remain paused. Source byte backups and central registration are completed for this delivery; no upload or saver/verifier restart at Archive.org is authorized or performed.
